{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel to Sparkling, the Customer)  
**Re:** Playbook review — Software License and Maintenance Agreement  

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook and identified **18 findings: 3 critical, 6 high, 8 medium and 1 low**. Of these, **9 are deviations**, **3 are missing terms** and **6 are already compliant**.

The three critical items sit in the risk-allocation core of the deal. **Section 15** contains no aggregate liability cap at all and is drafted as a limitation of Garman's liability only, without express uncapped carve-outs for gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, data protection/security or IP infringement. **Section 13** gives us a narrow IP indemnity tied only to the ownership/non-infringement warranty, with no duty to defend, no affiliate coverage and nothing for breach of law, data incidents or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. The same section vests ownership of all IP in the Work — including the Schedule "D" Modifications we paid for — in Garman, with a sweep-up broad enough to capture our own inputs and data.

At the high level, the assignment regime (Section 20(d), reinforced by Section 3(c) and the "non-transferable" grant in Section 2) imposes blanket consent with no affiliate or M&A carve-out for us, which is a walk-away position and also undermines the licence grant on a corporate transaction. Our convenience right under Section 17(b) works but runs on 90 days' notice with no refund of prepaid maintenance fees.

Medium items are largely gap-filling: Nova Scotia governing law and non-exclusive jurisdiction fall outside our accepted list; maintenance renewal mechanics and renewal-fee protection are absent; there is no Garman-side transition assistance or return/deletion of our data on termination; the Section 12 warranty carries no remedy and no services, malicious code or compliance warranties; and Section 19 is a mutual **no-hire** rather than a non-solicit. There is no insurance clause anywhere in the Agreement.

Helpfully, the Agreement is clean on several fronts we often have to fight: no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation, no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, no non-compete or field-of-use covenant, no vendor audit right against our usage, no MFN and no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment.

*Note: automated verification was skipped for all findings below; each rests on the reviewer's rationale as recorded.*

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Page 10 |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 17 Term and Termination |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Page 10 |
| 11 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Deviation | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees |
| 12 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 12 Specifications and Warranty |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Missing | § 10 Maintenance and Support |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 17 Term and Termination |
| 15 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use |
| 16 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees |
| 17 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 11 Fees |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Page 11 |

### Positions taken on the deviations and gaps

- **§ 13 (indemnity):** we add a Garman defence and indemnity for IP infringement, breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Sparkling data, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, together with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics. Section 15 already carves Section 13 out of the liability limitation, so the cap is not an obstacle here.
- **§ 13 (IP ownership):** we take the playbook fallback given the object-code/escrow bargain — Garman keeps its platform IP, our data and supplied materials are carved out, we take a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to the Modifications and Improvements we pay for, and joint ownership is excluded.
- **§ 15:** we add a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, an Excluded Claims definition (preserving the existing Section 13/14 carve-out), exclusion of our payment obligations from the cap, and a mutual heading. Fallback: a plain mutual 12 months' fees cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
- **§ 20(d) / § 3(c) / § 2:** affiliate and successor assignment carve-out for us; Garman's assignment subject to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and not to our competitors; confirmation that a change of control of Sparkling is not an assignment and triggers no termination or re-pricing right.
- **§ 2:** extend the licence to contractors acting on our behalf and permit transfer to a successor.
- **§ 17(b):** 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Fallback: 60 days, provided the refund is preserved.
- **Governing law:** New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County. There is no arbitration clause, so only the jurisdiction words and forum change.
- **§ 19:** narrow to a 12-month mutual non-solicit running from the end of an individual's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and express confirmation that hiring is not prohibited. Survival under Section 18 remains acceptable for the narrowed clause.
- **§ 12:** add a professional and workmanlike services warranty (installation, data conversion, training, maintenance), malicious code and legal compliance warranties, and a repair/replace-then-refund remedy, confirming the warranty is not displaced by fee-bearing Section 10 maintenance.
- **§ 10:** add 12-month renewal terms we may decline on 30 days' notice, a 60-day Garman reminder, and a cap on renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%. Fallback: 60-day window and 5% cap.
- **New § 17(d):** six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in machine-readable form within 30 days and post-return deletion certification, added to the Section 18 survival list.
- **New § 20(k):** short vendor insurance covenant in General Matters, after the entire-agreement subsection.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

Two findings engage express playbook walk-away positions:

1. **Assignment — blanket consent with no affiliate or M&A carve-out (Section 20(d), reinforced by Section 3(c) and the "non-transferable" grant in Section 2).** A consent requirement with no reasonableness standard and no carve-out for our affiliates or successors is our walk-away position; combined with the licence terms it would leave the licence unusable on a corporate transaction.
2. **Section 19 — mutual no-hire covering "any employee of the other party" for the term plus one year.** No-hire provisions covering all of the counterparty's personnel are a walk-away. Because the restriction is mutual and part of the existing bargain, we propose narrowing to the fallback non-solicit rather than deletion.

We also flag the three critical items (Sections 13 and 15) as must-fix: an unlimited, one-sided liability regime combined with a narrow indemnity and Garman ownership of the Modifications we paid for is not a package we can recommend signing as drafted.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the nine deviations and three missing terms, prefixed `[Playbook]`, leading with Sections 13, 15, 17 and the assignment and governing-law provisions.
2. **Obtain Schedule "A" (Fee Schedule) and Schedule "D".** The Fee Schedule was not in the reviewed text; we must confirm it contains no minimum quantities and no non-refundable multi-year prepayments before relying on the MINCOMMIT and LD findings.
3. **Confirm the commercial mandate** on the liability cap figure (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) and on the renewal uplift cap, so we know which fallbacks we may concede.
4. **Escalate the two walk-away items** to the business owner ahead of negotiation, so we are aligned on the consequence if Garman refuses the affiliate/M&A carve-out or the narrowed non-solicit.
5. **Preserve the compliant positions.** No exclusivity, liquidated damages, non-compete, MFN, minimum commitment or vendor audit right currently binds us; we should resist any "reciprocal" additions in these areas, and in particular should not introduce audit machinery Garman does not presently have.
6. **Run verification** on the findings before the redline is sent externally, as verification was skipped in this pass.
"}
